characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Through-thickness embedding, grinding and polishing performed separately for hot-rolled and heat-treated samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyse all the alloys at the different processing conditions (hot-rolling and tempering)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 5 kg load applied for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure macro-hardness of the alloys in the hot-rolled and tempered conditions

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Composition 9Al-10Mn-1C (wt%); temperature axis 0–1300 °C; output amount of all phases [mol] (0.00–1.10); phases FCC_A1, BCC_A2, KAPPA_E21
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic equilibrium calculation of phase volume fractions (amount of all phases [mol] vs temperature [°C])
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Used qualitatively to explain thermodynamic gradients in austenite stability; the text notes hot-rolled conditions at T are not the same as during hot-rolling at 1150 °C, so the comparison is described as indicative and qualitative only

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Different alloyed steels were produced by casting using a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, resulting in 0.5 kg ingots (composition within Table 1).
Ingots were hot-rolled at 1150 °C, obtaining 5 mm flat-products.
Hot-rolled flat products were followed by water quenching; this defines the as-received hot-rolled state.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers macro-hardness; 5 kg load; 5 indentations per sample; hot-rolled (as-received) condition

unmapped_findings: The 9Al-10Mn-1C composition lies within the tested composition ranges of Table 1: Al 9–12 wt%, Mn 10–20–30 wt%, C 0.4–1 wt%, Fe balance.

No micrograph or morphological description of the as-hot-rolled 9Al-10Mn-1C condition is given in the paper; all reported microstructures (discontinuous precipitation at 600 °C, precipitation transformation, cellular transformation and spinodal decomposition at 800 °C) belong to the 600 °C/800 °C tempered samples and must not be attributed to this hot-rolled sample.

The hot-rolled 9Al-10Mn-1C hardness of 273 HV serves as the as-received reference/baseline in the tempering comparisons of Tables 2 (600 °C, 439 HV), 5 and 8 (800 °C, 356 HV) and Table 9 (600 °C, inter-lamellar spacing 'Narrow').

Minitab18® software was used to verify the consistency of the acquired hardness data (outliers excluded) and to plot data highlighting chemical composition and process effects; this data-analysis step is not specific to the hot-rolled condition.
